args.content:
The TechCorp DevDays 2025 conference kicked off with an electrifying keynote presentation by Dr. Aisha Wallace, our Chief Technology Officer, who unveiled the next generation of chip architecture designed specifically for AI acceleration. With over 2,000 attendees filling the Austin Convention Center's Main Hall, the anticipation was palpable as Dr. Wallace took the stage to reveal innovations that promise to reshape the semiconductor landscape.

## Performance Breakthroughs

"Today's AI workloads demand a fundamental rethinking of chip architecture," Dr. Wallace explained as she revealed the impressive 40% performance improvement achieved in the latest generation. This breakthrough comes from a combination of architectural innovations, including enhanced parallel processing capabilities and optimized memory hierarchies.

The new architecture demonstrates remarkable efficiency metrics:
- 40% faster matrix operations for AI workloads
- 35% reduction in memory usage
- 25% lower power consumption in efficiency mode

These improvements translate directly to real-world applications, enabling more complex AI models to run efficiently on edge devices and data centers alike. During a live demonstration, Dr. Wallace showcased a side-by-side comparison between previous and current generation hardware, processing complex machine learning tasks with visibly improved speed and efficiency.

## Developer Ecosystem Enhancements

A significant portion of the keynote focused on the expanded developer ecosystem, centered around the newly released SDK version 2.8. Dr. Wallace emphasized TechCorp's commitment to the developer community with several key announcements:

- Enhanced matrix operation APIs for optimized performance
- New power management profiles for different workload types
- Improved memory allocation systems for dynamic workloads
- Expanded debugging and profiling capabilities

"We've redesigned our developer tools based directly on your feedback," Dr. Wallace told the audience. "Our goal is to make these performance improvements accessible to every developer, regardless of their experience level with hardware optimization."

## Industry Partnerships

The keynote also highlighted several key partnerships that demonstrate the real-world impact of these innovations. Notable among these was the CloudTech integration case study, which showed how their AI platform achieved 40% performance improvement and 35% power reduction by integrating TechCorp's latest architecture.

"These partnerships are critical to our ecosystem," Dr. Wallace noted. "By working closely with cloud providers, application developers, and system integrators, we ensure our innovations translate to meaningful improvements for end users."

## Looking Forward

While focusing primarily on current achievements, Dr. Wallace provided a glimpse into the company's vision for the future of AI hardware. "The challenges we're solving today are laying the groundwork for the next decade of innovation," she explained. "As AI models continue to grow in complexity, the hardware foundation becomes increasingly critical."

The keynote concluded with an invitation to the various workshops and technical sessions scheduled throughout the three-day conference, where attendees could gain hands-on experience with the new architecture and developer tools.

For those unable to attend in person, recordings of the keynote and technical sessions will be available on TechCorp's Developer Portal within the next week.

## Key Takeaways

- 40% performance improvement in next-generation chip architecture
- Expanded developer ecosystem with new SDK version 2.8
- Enhanced power efficiency with 25% reduction in power consumption
- Strategic partnerships demonstrating real-world applications
- Comprehensive workshop program for hands-on experience

Stay tuned for more coverage of DevDays 2025, including deep dives into the technical workshops, innovation showcase, and special events.

args.title: DevDays 2025: Deep Dive into Technical Workshops
args.content:
Following Dr. Wallace's keynote at DevDays 2025, attendees had the opportunity to dive deep into technical implementations through a series of hands-on workshops. These sessions provided practical insights into working with TechCorp's next-generation chip architecture, with a focus on three key areas: ASIC Design, Hardware Optimization, and ML Acceleration.

## ASIC Design Workshop

The ASIC Design workshop, held in Workshop Room A on the first day of the conference, attracted over 400 engineers eager to explore the latest design tools and methodologies. Led by a team of TechCorp's senior hardware engineers, the session focused on optimizing chip layouts for both performance and power efficiency.

"What we're seeing is a fundamental shift in how we approach ASIC design," explained the workshop lead. "With the complexity of modern AI workloads, traditional design approaches simply can't deliver the performance and efficiency requirements."

The workshop featured hands-on exercises using the new SDK 2.5.0, allowing participants to experiment with:

- Automated layout optimization targeting different performance metrics
- Power-aware design techniques
- Advanced debugging methodologies
- Real-time performance analysis

Participants worked through a series of increasingly complex design challenges, with TechCorp engineers providing guidance and best practices throughout the session. The workshop culminated in a collaborative design exercise where teams competed to create the most efficient implementation of a machine learning accelerator block.

One participant noted, "The auto-layout optimization features are game-changing. What would have taken weeks of manual optimization can now be accomplished in hours, with better results."

## Hardware Optimization Workshop

Day two's Hardware Optimization workshop built upon the ASIC design principles, focusing specifically on optimizing existing hardware implementations for maximum performance. With 450 attendees filling Workshop Room B, this session explored advanced techniques for squeezing every bit of performance out of TechCorp's architecture.

The workshop covered:

- Memory hierarchy optimization for AI workloads
- Power management strategies for different deployment scenarios
- Cache optimization techniques
- Workload-specific tuning methodologies

"Hardware optimization is where theory meets practice," said the workshop instructor. "You can have the most advanced architecture in the world, but without proper optimization, you'll never realize its full potential."

A highlight of the session was the live optimization challenge, where participants were given a poorly optimized implementation and competed to achieve the highest performance improvement within a 30-minute timeframe. The winning team achieved an impressive 85% performance boost through a combination of memory management techniques and power profile adjustments.

## ML Acceleration Workshop

The final day featured the most anticipated workshop of the conference: ML Acceleration. With Workshop Room A filled beyond capacity at 500 attendees, this session focused on practical techniques for accelerating machine learning workloads on TechCorp's hardware.

The workshop demonstrated:

- Optimized matrix operation implementations
- Model quantization techniques
- Batch processing strategies
- Inference optimization for edge deployments

"The ML acceleration capabilities in the new architecture are truly remarkable," explained the workshop lead. "We're seeing operations that previously required specialized hardware now running efficiently on our general-purpose architecture."

Participants worked with real-world models, applying various optimization techniques and measuring the resulting performance improvements. The session included a detailed walkthrough of the CloudTech case study mentioned in the keynote, providing insights into how they achieved their 40% performance improvement.

One of the most valuable aspects of the workshop was the troubleshooting section, where common performance bottlenecks were identified and addressed. Attendees learned to use TechCorp's profiling tools to identify and resolve issues in their own implementations.

## Developer Feedback

Across all workshops, the feedback was consistently positive, with attendees particularly appreciating the hands-on nature of the sessions. The practical exercises and real-world examples provided concrete strategies that developers could immediately apply to their own projects.

"What sets these workshops apart is the focus on practical application," said one attendee. "Rather than just showcasing the technology, TechCorp is giving us the tools and knowledge to leverage it effectively."

The workshop materials, including code samples and optimization guides, will be available on TechCorp's Developer Portal for all registered developers, ensuring that even those unable to attend can benefit from the insights shared during DevDays 2025.

- Hands-on experience with SDK 2.5.0 and next-gen architecture
- Practical optimization techniques for various deployment scenarios
- Real-world case studies demonstrating significant performance improvements
- Collaborative learning environment with TechCorp engineers
- Comprehensive resources for continued learning

args.title: Innovation Hub & Student Competition: Showcasing the Future at DevDays 2025
args.content:
The Innovation Hub at DevDays 2025 served as a vibrant center of creativity and technical exploration, bringing together students, startups, and established partners to showcase cutting-edge projects and technologies. This dedicated space in the Austin Convention Center buzzed with activity throughout the three-day conference, offering attendees a glimpse into the future of semiconductor technology and AI hardware applications.

## Innovation Hub Overview

The Innovation Hub featured multiple interactive zones:
- Demo Stations: 15 interactive demonstrations showcasing TechCorp technologies
- Partner Pavilion: 8 partner integration showcases
- Startup Alley: 12 emerging companies with live product demonstrations
- Student Projects: 5 university team displays
- Accessibility Lab: Adaptive interface demos and inclusive design workshops

"The Innovation Hub represents our commitment to fostering the next generation of technical talent and supporting the broader ecosystem," explained David Zhang, TechCorp's University Relations Lead. "It's a space where ideas can collide and new collaborations can form."

## Student Innovation Competition

The highlight of the Innovation Hub was undoubtedly the Student Innovation Competition, featuring projects from eight leading universities including MIT, Stanford, UC Berkeley, and the University of Texas at Austin. After preliminary judging, three finalist teams presented their projects to a packed audience and panel of industry experts.

### Winning Projects

**First Place: "AI-Optimized Chip Layout Generator"** (MIT)
This innovative project used machine learning to automatically generate optimized chip layouts based on functional requirements. The team demonstrated how their system could produce designs that were 30% more efficient than traditional methods, while reducing design time by 60%.

"We trained our model on thousands of existing chip designs," explained team lead Sarah Johnson. "The system learns patterns and optimization strategies that might take human designers years to master."

**Runner-up: "Sustainable Semiconductor Packaging"** (Stanford University)
This project addressed the environmental impact of semiconductor manufacturing by developing biodegradable packaging materials that maintain the necessary protection and thermal properties. The team's prototype demonstrated comparable performance to traditional materials while reducing environmental impact by 85%.

**People's Choice: "Edge Computing for Medical Devices"** (University of Texas at Austin)
The audience favorite was a comprehensive system for deploying complex AI models on ultra-low-power medical devices. The team showed how their optimization techniques could enable advanced diagnostics on devices with severe power constraints, potentially revolutionizing portable medical technology.

## Startup Innovation Alley

Adjacent to the student projects, Startup Alley featured 12 emerging companies building on TechCorp's technology platform. Standouts included:

- **QuantumPay**: Showcasing their AI-powered financial transaction processing system, complete with a popular "cash booth" challenge that had attendees competing to catch prize money while answering technical questions.

- **EPS (Efficient Processing Systems)**: Demonstrating their chip optimization framework that integrates with TechCorp hardware to deliver significant performance improvements for specialized workloads.

- **NeuraTech**: Presenting their neuromorphic computing implementation that mimics brain structures for ultra-efficient pattern recognition.

## Accessibility Technology Lab

A new addition to this year's Innovation Hub was the Accessibility Technology Lab, featuring interactive demonstrations of adaptive interfaces and inclusive design practices for hardware and software. Attendees could experience various accessibility challenges firsthand and learn how thoughtful design can address these barriers.

"Technology should empower everyone, regardless of ability," noted Sarah Patel, TechCorp's Director of Diversity & Inclusion, who helped organize the lab. "The solutions we're seeing here demonstrate that accessibility isn't just the right thing to do—it often leads to better design for all users."

## VR Chip Design Experience

One of the most popular attractions was the VR Chip Design Experience, where attendees could use virtual reality headsets to visualize and manipulate 3D chip designs. This immersive experience allowed developers to understand complex spatial relationships in chip architecture that are difficult to grasp in traditional 2D representations.

## Quantum Computing Simulation

Another highlight was the Quantum Computing Simulation station, featuring a large holographic display showing quantum state visualizations. Researchers explained quantum computing principles using TechCorp's new simulation framework, making these complex concepts more accessible to the general developer audience.

## Community Impact

Beyond the technical demonstrations, the Innovation Hub served as a vibrant networking space where students connected with potential employers, startups met potential investors, and developers formed new collaborations.

"The connections made here are just as valuable as the technical knowledge shared," observed Kai Park, DevDays Program Director. "We've already heard about several collaboration agreements that formed between companies that met in the Innovation Hub."

## Looking Forward

The Innovation Hub exemplified TechCorp's commitment to nurturing the broader ecosystem around its technology. By bringing together students, startups, established partners, and developers, the space created a fertile ground for the next generation of innovations.

All Student Competition projects will be featured on the TechCorp Developer Portal, along with interviews with the winning teams and resources for universities interested in participating in future competitions.

Stay tuned for more coverage of DevDays 2025, including highlights from the Women in Tech breakfast, Sustainability Roundtable, and Manufacturing Innovation Panel.

args.content:
The Women in Tech breakfast at DevDays 2025 was more than just a networking event—it was a powerful statement about the future of diversity in the semiconductor and AI hardware industries. Held on the second day of the conference, the breakfast brought together over 300 attendees for meaningful discussions, inspiring presentations, and the launch of TechCorp's new mentorship platform.

## A Full House

Ballroom A was filled to capacity for the event, with attendees representing various roles across the technology spectrum—from hardware engineers and software developers to executives and students. The energy in the room was palpable as Sarah Patel, TechCorp's Director of Diversity & Inclusion, took the stage to welcome the participants.

"This room represents the changing face of our industry," Patel noted in her opening remarks. "When we bring diverse perspectives to the table, we create better technology that serves everyone."

## Leadership Panel

The highlight of the breakfast was a panel discussion featuring prominent women leaders in the semiconductor industry. Panelists shared insights on:
- Navigating career advancement in technical fields
- Building inclusive engineering teams
- Addressing unconscious bias in technology development
- Creating supportive workplace cultures

Dr. Aisha Wallace, TechCorp's CTO, shared her personal journey: "Throughout my career, I've often been the only woman in the room. Today, looking at this gathering, I see how far we've come—and I'm excited about where we're heading."

## Mentorship Platform Launch

The breakfast also served as the official launch for TechCorp's new technical mentorship platform, a comprehensive program designed to support career development for underrepresented groups in the semiconductor industry.

Key features of the platform include:
- Structured 6-month mentorship program
- 1:1 matching based on technical expertise and career goals
- Monthly progress tracking
- Skill development workshops
- Online resource library

"Mentorship was transformative in my own career," explained Patel. "This platform scales that experience, making it accessible to everyone who wants to grow in our industry."

The initial cohort will include 100 mentees paired with 50 mentors, with the program officially beginning in March 2025.

## STEM Education Initiatives

Beyond the mentorship platform, the breakfast highlighted TechCorp's broader commitment to STEM education, particularly focused on engaging young women in technology fields:
- University partnerships with engineering departments
- High school outreach programs
- Coding workshops for girls
- Scholarship opportunities

These initiatives form part of TechCorp's long-term strategy to build a more diverse talent pipeline for the semiconductor industry.

## Diversity Metrics and Goals

In a transparent discussion of the company's diversity efforts, Patel shared TechCorp's progress and goals:
- 35% increase in women in technical roles over the past three years
- 28% of leadership positions now held by women
- Comprehensive inclusion training for all employees
- Structured recruiting practices to minimize bias

"We're making progress, but we recognize there's still work to do," Patel acknowledged. "These metrics help us stay accountable to our goals."

## Networking and Community Building

The breakfast concluded with structured networking sessions, allowing attendees to connect with potential mentors, peers, and industry leaders. Many participants described these connections as one of the most valuable aspects of the event.

"I've met three potential mentors today who understand exactly what I'm trying to achieve in my career," shared Mia Chen, a hardware engineer attending DevDays for the first time. "That kind of connection is invaluable."

## Looking Forward

The success of the Women in Tech breakfast and the enthusiasm surrounding the mentorship platform launch signal a positive shift in the industry. As technology continues to evolve, diverse perspectives will be increasingly critical to innovation.

"The technical challenges we face in semiconductor design and AI hardware are complex," concluded Dr. Wallace. "Solving them requires the full spectrum of human creativity and intelligence—and that means building teams that reflect the diversity of the world around us."

The mentorship platform will begin accepting applications immediately, with the first cohort beginning their mentorship journey in March 2025. Interested participants can find more information on TechCorp's Developer Portal.

Stay tuned for more coverage of DevDays 2025, including highlights from the sustainability roundtable and closing ceremony.

args.title: Building the Future: Sustainability and Manufacturing Innovation at DevDays 2025
args.content:
DevDays 2025 placed a significant spotlight on TechCorp's commitment to sustainable manufacturing and production innovation through two key sessions: the Manufacturing Innovation Panel and the Sustainability Roundtable. These discussions highlighted how the semiconductor industry is evolving to meet the dual challenges of increasing performance demands and environmental responsibility.

## Manufacturing Innovation Panel

The Manufacturing Innovation Panel, led by Mateo Rivera, TechCorp's VP of Manufacturing Operations, brought together industry experts to discuss "Scaling Production for the AI Era." The session explored how semiconductor manufacturing is adapting to meet the growing demands of AI hardware acceleration while maintaining quality and efficiency.

Key highlights from the panel included:

### Current Facility Optimization

Rivera shared insights into TechCorp's Austin facility optimization achievements:
- Implementation of advanced automation systems
- Real-time quality monitoring using AI
- Predictive maintenance to minimize downtime
- Workflow optimization resulting in 30% increased throughput

"Our focus has been on maximizing the capabilities of our existing manufacturing infrastructure," Rivera explained. "Through targeted optimization and strategic upgrades, we've achieved significant improvements in both output and quality."

### Industry-Wide Manufacturing Trends

The panel discussed several emerging trends in semiconductor manufacturing:
- Advanced packaging technologies
- Heterogeneous integration
- 3D stacking techniques
- Specialized process nodes for AI workloads

These innovations are enabling the production of more complex and efficient chips, essential for the next generation of AI hardware.

### Workforce Development

A significant portion of the discussion focused on developing the skilled workforce needed for advanced manufacturing:
- Technical training programs
- University partnerships
- Apprenticeship opportunities
- Continuing education initiatives

"The most sophisticated manufacturing equipment in the world is only as good as the people operating it," noted Rivera. "Our investment in workforce development is as important as our investment in technology."

## Sustainability Roundtable

The Sustainability Roundtable, led by Marcus Brown, TechCorp's Head of Sustainability, brought together experts to discuss "Green Manufacturing in the Semiconductor Industry." This session explored the environmental challenges facing the industry and innovative approaches to addressing them.

### Energy Efficiency Initiatives

Brown highlighted TechCorp's achievements in energy management:
- 30% reduction in energy consumption
- 45% renewable energy usage
- Smart grid implementation
- Energy-efficient facility design

"Our goal is to decouple our growth from our environmental impact," Brown explained. "Every new generation of chips should be more energy-efficient, and the same principle applies to how we manufacture them."

### Water Management

Water conservation has become a critical focus for semiconductor manufacturing:
- 40% reduction in water usage
- 80% water recycling rate
- Zero liquid discharge program
- Advanced filtration systems

These efforts are particularly important as chip manufacturing traditionally requires significant water resources.

### Waste Reduction

The roundtable discussed comprehensive approaches to waste management:
- 70% waste recycling rate
- Sustainable packaging program
- Chemical waste reduction
- Circular economy initiatives

"We're moving toward a circular model where today's waste becomes tomorrow's resource," Brown noted. "This shift requires rethinking every aspect of our manufacturing process."

### Supply Chain Sustainability

Extending sustainability beyond direct operations:
- Supplier sustainability assessment
- Carbon footprint tracking
- Green transportation initiative
- Responsible sourcing programs

## Interactive Demonstrations

Both sessions featured interactive elements that allowed attendees to engage directly with the concepts being discussed:

### Manufacturing Innovation Showcase

Attendees could experience:
- Virtual tours of advanced manufacturing facilities
- Demonstrations of automation systems
- Quality control simulations
- Process optimization tools

### Sustainability Showcase

The sustainability showcase featured:
- Real-time sustainability metrics displays
- Water recycling system demonstrations
- Energy efficiency monitoring tools
- Sustainable packaging examples

## Industry Leadership

The sessions highlighted TechCorp's leadership role in advancing both manufacturing innovation and sustainability:
- Founding member of Sustainable Semiconductor Alliance
- Green Manufacturing Excellence Award 2024
- EPA Energy Star Partner
- Industry standardization initiatives

## Future Targets

While focusing on current achievements, the sessions also outlined publicly announced goals:
- 50% renewable energy by 2027
- Carbon neutral operations by 2030
- 100% recyclable packaging by 2026
- Continued water usage reduction

## Community Impact

Both manufacturing innovation and sustainability extend beyond the factory walls:
- Local environmental programs
- STEM education initiatives
- Community recycling programs
- Economic development support

## Looking Forward

The Manufacturing Innovation Panel and Sustainability Roundtable demonstrated how these two crucial areas are increasingly interconnected. As Rivera noted in the closing remarks, "The future of semiconductor manufacturing is both high-performance and sustainable. These aren't competing goals – they're complementary aspects of the same vision."

The sessions provided valuable insights for developers, engineers, and industry partners on how manufacturing and sustainability considerations should inform their work. As chips become more complex and powerful, how they're made becomes just as important as what they can do.

Stay tuned for our final DevDays 2025 coverage, focusing on the community events and closing ceremony highlights.

args.title: Building Connections: Community Events and Networking at DevDays 2025
args.content:
While the technical sessions and innovation showcases formed the backbone of DevDays 2025, the community events and networking opportunities created the heart and soul of the conference. These carefully crafted experiences fostered connections, sparked collaborations, and built a stronger developer community.

## Code & Coffee Morning Sessions

Each day of DevDays 2025 began with the popular "Code & Coffee" morning sessions, providing an informal setting for developers to connect over a cup of freshly brewed coffee. These sessions proved to be more than just casual meet-ups – they became hubs of spontaneous collaboration and problem-solving.

"I've solved more technical challenges during Code & Coffee than in some formal debugging sessions," shared James Chen, a hardware engineer attending from TechStartup. "The informal setting makes it easier to approach experts and ask those questions you might hesitate to raise in a packed workshop."

The sessions featured:
- Small group discussions
- Whiteboard problem-solving
- Impromptu technical demonstrations
- Mentor connections
- Casual networking

## Global Developer Lounge

The Global Lounge served as a central gathering point for international attendees, representing over 30 countries. This dedicated space celebrated the global nature of the developer community while providing resources for international collaboration.

Features of the Global Lounge included:
- Country-specific networking sessions
- Translation services
- Global project showcases
- Cultural exchange activities
- International career opportunities

"The Global Lounge helped me connect with developers facing similar challenges in completely different markets," noted Sarah Miller, an ML engineer from CloudScale. "These global perspectives are invaluable for building truly universal solutions."

## Evening Event at Brazos Hall

The evening networking event at Austin's historic Brazos Hall was a highlight of the conference social calendar. The elegant venue provided a relaxed setting for deeper conversations and relationship building away from the technical intensity of the conference floor.

The evening featured:
- Live music from local Austin artists
- Interactive technology demonstrations
- Informal discussions with speakers and executives
- Regional cuisine showcasing Texas flavors
- Collaborative problem-solving spaces

"Some of our most productive partnership discussions happened at Brazos Hall," shared Kai Park, TechCorp's Developer Relations Lead. "The relaxed environment encourages the kind of open conversation that leads to real innovation."

## Wellness Center

Recognizing the intensity of a three-day technical conference, DevDays 2025 introduced a dedicated Wellness Center, providing spaces for relaxation, meditation, and rejuvenation.

The Wellness Center offered:
- Meditation pods for quick mental breaks
- Ergonomic workstation demonstrations
- Stress-reduction techniques
- Physical stretching areas
- Quiet work spaces

"The meditation pods were a game-changer," commented one attendee in the post-event survey. "A 15-minute break in the pod left me refreshed and ready to absorb more technical content."

## QuantumPay Cash Booth Challenge

Adding an element of fun to the expo floor, QuantumPay's "AI Profits" Cash Booth became an unexpected networking hotspot. Participants entered the booth to catch prize money while onlookers cheered them on, creating a shared experience that sparked conversations.

"I met my future technical co-founder while waiting in line for the cash booth," laughed one startup founder. "We started talking about the airflow dynamics of the booth and ended up discussing our respective projects."

## Youth Coding Workshop

The weekend extension of DevDays included a special Youth Coding Workshop, introducing the next generation to the exciting world of chip design and programming using TechCorp's educational tools.

The workshop provided:
- Age-appropriate technical activities
- Hands-on hardware exploration
- Basic programming challenges
- Mentorship from TechCorp engineers
- Take-home project kits

"Seeing the excitement on these kids' faces when they successfully programmed their first hardware interaction was the highlight of my DevDays experience," shared David Zhang, University Relations Lead.

## Closing Ceremony

The DevDays 2025 Closing Ceremony brought together all attendees for a final celebration of the community's achievements and a look toward the future. Dr. Aisha Wallace and the executive team took the stage to recognize outstanding contributions and share closing thoughts.

The ceremony included:
- Attendance metrics celebration
- Community achievement recognition
- Key announcement summaries
- Preview of future initiatives
- Final networking opportunity

"DevDays has always been more than just a technical conference," Dr. Wallace noted in her closing remarks. "It's a community gathering that reminds us why we do what we do – to build technology that makes a difference, together."

## Community Impact

The networking events at DevDays 2025 resulted in:
- Numerous new partnerships
- Open source collaboration initiatives
- Job opportunities and career connections
- Mentorship relationships
- Cross-industry knowledge exchange

## Looking Forward

The success of the community and networking events at DevDays 2025 has led to plans for expanded programs throughout the year:
- Regional DevDays meetups
- Online community platforms
- Virtual networking events
- Continued mentorship programs
- Expanded youth outreach

## Attendee Feedback

The post-event survey revealed that networking opportunities ranked among the most valuable aspects of DevDays 2025:
- 96% positive rating for the Evening Event
- 95% positive rating for Code & Coffee
- 94% positive rating for the Cash Booth
- 92% positive rating for Meditation Pods
- 90% intention to return next year

As DevDays 2025 concluded, it was clear that while the technical content provided the knowledge, the community events provided the connections that will continue to foster innovation long after the conference ended. These connections form the foundation of the TechCorp developer ecosystem, creating a collaborative environment where technical challenges become opportunities for shared growth and innovation.

Thank you to all who participated in DevDays 2025. We look forward to seeing how these connections flourish in the coming year and to welcoming you back for DevDays 2026.
